blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Sedimentary rocks are created from accumulated sediments that undergo compaction and cementation over time.
These rocks characteristically feature distinct layers, also known as being stratified.
They frequently entrap organic remains, making them the primary rock type containing fossils.
Compared to igneous or metamorphic rocks, sedimentary rocks are relatively soft.
They form essential reserves for major fossil fuels, including coal, petroleum, and natural gas.
Fossils are almost exclusively preserved in sedimentary rocks due to their low-heat formation process.
Stratification (layered arrangement) is a defining feature frequently asked about in rock type identification questions.
Economic geography questions often link sedimentary rock formations to coal, petroleum, and natural gas deposits.
